subject: Intermittent on-prem route blackholing during hybrid cutover — SG divergence + MTU probe regression
messages:
From: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@clearsky.health>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Production cutover — intermittent blackholes after route import

Hi Vanessa,

We completed the initial phase of the hybrid cutover this morning (per the runbook) and are seeing intermittent TCP flows to the Redwood private gateway drop without obvious errors. Flows succeed, then 20s later packets stop and traceroutes from our on-prem app server show a next-hop that disappears (blackhole) inside the transit fabric.

Symptoms observed: 
- SYNs reach the gateway but SYN-ACK never returned for a handful of sessions.
- ICMP path MTU probes that used to work now either time out or show fragmentation inconsistently.
- When we scale our SNAT pool (ephemeral ports scale up) the window of failures increases.

I've attached a short pcap of a repro and rt-table diffs from the on-prem router. We suspect either a route import hiccup or an SG rule on the private gateway interface that was pushed with the wrong direction/bind and causes asymmetric pathing.

Can you triage? We are currently routing critical requests through a fallback region but need this resolved before traffic cutover continues.

Thanks,
Diego
Operations Lead, ClearSky Health
attachments: clearsky_pcap_probe_20271110.zip, rt-table-diff-20271110.txt
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@clearsky.health>, Nadia Petrov <nadia.petrov@clearsky.health>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover — intermittent blackholes after route import

Thanks Diego — taking this on. Initial read: two-pronged hypothesis (1) route import timing + ECMP hash causing transient next-hop disappearance, (2) SG policy that was intended for the management interface applied to the data-facing interface during the cutover push.

What I'll do now: 
- Kick off targeted MTU + ICMP probe from one of our gateway instances to your affected on-prem IPs.
- Ask infra to fetch the gateway kernel conntrack and SNAT counters during a repro window.
- Request the exact ACL/SG bundle that was applied at 07:30 cutover (Marissa: can you pull a policy export?)

Can you put the fallback region traffic on hold for 30 mins while we run a controlled probe? That will help correlate conntrack entries to repro attempts.

-Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Customer SR
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2027 08:41:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover — intermittent blackholes after route import

Vanessa — exported the policy bundle from the control plane and diffed it against the pre-cutover bundle. Key findings in rt-table-diff-20271111.txt and sg-policy-export-20271112.json (attached to this thread):

- There was a policy rename in the orchestration pipeline that changed the interface tag from private-data to private-data-legacy; the orchestration engine has a mapping but the mapping failed for one apply cycle (race condition). 
- As a result the management-only rule (deny from 10.0.0.0/24 to 0.0.0.0/0) was applied to the data interface for roughly 4 minutes.
- Also observed: our SNAT pool size doubled during autoscale at 07:35, and conntrack ephemeral port allocation spiked. Kernel logs show several NAT timeouts during that period.

Next steps I suggest: 
- Roll back the single failed policy apply (we have the previous bundle) to restore the intended interface tag.
- Run an MTU/PMTU sweep across the path while conntrack counters are monitored.
- Add a temporary rule to allow ICMP-frag-needed and traceroute traffic through the data interface for the repro window.

Marissa
Network Reliability Engineer
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Nadia Petrov <nadia.petrov@clearsky.health>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2027 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover — intermittent blackholes after route import

Looping in kernel/VPC team for conntrack analysis. Preliminary notes: 
- The combination of (a) interface-level SG deny + (b) burst SNAT port allocation can cause mid-flow asymmetry if return path pins to a different egress that doesn't have the same ephemeral port mapping; the symptom looks like a blackhole because the gateway drops packets with no conntrack match. 
- MTU probe timeouts could be a red herring if the gateway silently drops ICMP fragments when under conntrack pressure. Need to confirm whether netfilter is dropping frag-needed messages or whether those are being rate-limited by the appliance.

I recommend enabling a short-lived conntrack sampling trace on the gateway, and temporarily expanding the SNAT timeout to reduce churn during repro. I've created a lightweight trace command that we can run (won't impact throughput): 
- sudo nft monitor | grep conntrack (run in a controlled window)

I'll also check the kernel NAT timeout defaults and propose a temporary increase.

Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@clearsky.health>, Nadia Petrov <nadia.petrov@clearsky.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2027 09:55:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover — intermittent blackholes after route import

Diego/Nadia — thanks for the quick response and for blocking fallback traffic. Summary of actions so far: 
- Rolled back the single failed policy apply at 08:10 PT (removed management rule from data interface). 
- Enabled temporary ICMP-frag-needed allow and started conntrack sampling on the gateway. 
- Increased SNAT ephemeral port timeout from 30s -> 120s for the repro window. 

We ran controlled probes between 08:30 and 08:45. Results: 
- During the window when SNAT scaled, we observed 12 sessions where SYN reached the gateway but the reply hit a different egress and was dropped due to missing conntrack entry.
- PMTU probes showed intermittent ICMP timeouts during heavy conntrack churn but continued to succeed once ephemeral timeouts were extended.

Temporary mitigation: keep the SNAT timeout increase in place until we ship a config fix, and add a guard in the orchestration pipeline to fail safely if an interface tag rename maps to a different target.

We'll prepare a patch for the orchestration engine (Marissa + Karthik) and schedule a follow-up deploy that includes: 
- policy-apply guardrails + idempotent tagging
- conntrack backpressure metrics to surface this earlier
- a PMTU probe check as part of the cutover smoke tests

Vanessa
From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.ramos@clearsky.health>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 16:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Production cutover — intermittent blackholes after route import

Thanks team for the fast triage and for keeping ClearSky updated. Couple quick asks from leadership: 
- We need a short postmortem by EOD Wednesday that includes root cause, timeline, impact (RPS and failed sessions during the window), and the permanent remediation plan with rollout timeline. 
- Please include a short customer-facing blurb Vanessa can share with ClearSky summarizing the mitigation and ETA for the permanent fix.

Vanessa: can you coordinate the PM and author the customer note? Karthik/Marissa: pair on the remediation PR and include e2e smoke tests for PMTU and SNAT scale. Sergio: make sure the ops playbook is updated with the temporary SNAT timeout step as an emergency fallback.

Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
